Consult Summary:
- Patient Michael John presents with 3 days of acute diarrhea (4–5 stools/day), associated with mild abdominal pain, one episode of vomiting, and mild decreased appetite; management advice given for supportive care and return precautions.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Acute diarrhea for approximately 3 days.
  - Frequency: 4–5 bowel movements per day.
  - Stool character: intermittently watery and loose depending on time of day; no blood or mucus reported.
  - Associated symptoms: mild abdominal pain, one episode of vomiting, possible low-grade fever, decreased appetite.
  - Hydration/oral intake: able to drink; doctor visually assessed patient as not dehydrated.
- Timeline/progression:
  - Symptoms began ~3 days ago and have persisted; patient reports prior intermittent diarrhea historically after certain foods or travel, but no recent travel or dietary changes this episode.
  - Patient reports symptoms have “kept up” (no clear improvement documented).
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - No specific exacerbating or relieving factors identified.
  - No new or “dodgy” food eaten and no recent travel.
- Systems review / pertinent negatives:
  - No blood in stool.
  - No mucus in stool.
  - No additional systemic symptoms documented beyond possible low-grade fever and vomiting.
  - No other organ-system complaints documented.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma:
  - Patient reports a history of asthma and is uncertain of current status (“Probably I had asthma… I guess I still have it”).
  - Assessment/complications: none documented.
- Family history:
  - Father had hypertension and died of bowel cancer at age 62.

Medications:
- Inhaler described by patient as “Lexapro” (yellow) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Note: provider could not identify the named inhaler in the consult.
- No other medications or over-the-counter treatments reported or taken for current illness.
- Allergies:
  - Patient reports no known allergies.

Social History:
- Residence: confirmatory address obtained in London.
- Smoking, alcohol, recreational drug use:
  - Not documented in the consult.
- Occupational/financial/lifestyle factors:
  - No relevant details documented.

Family History:
- Father: hypertension; died of bowel cancer at age 62.
- No other family history documented.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: none documented.
- General appearance: provider noted patient “looks like you’re not dehydrated” (visual assessment).
- Other exam findings: none documented.

Investigations:
- No investigations ordered or results documented.
- Stool sample recommended if blood appears or if diarrhea persists >1 week (advice only; sample not collected).

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute diarrheal illness (3 days duration; 4–5 stools/day) with mild abdominal pain and one episode of vomiting
  - Assessment:
    - Likely self-limiting acute gastroenteritis given history and current symptoms; patient able to maintain oral intake and appears not dehydrated on visual assessment.
  - Plan:
    - Maintain adequate oral fluids; encourage oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte) to replace salts.
    - Dietary advice: soft/bland diet (e.g., crackers, toast, jam, mashed boiled vegetables) and avoid dairy, meat, fish, and eggs while symptomatic; can reintroduce meat/egg/fish after ~48 hours symptom-free.
    - Probiotic recommendation: yogurt is acceptable to help restore gut flora.
    - Return precautions: seek medical attention and submit stool sample if passing blood or if diarrhea persists >1 week; seek urgent care/hospital if stool frequency increases to ~6–8 times/day or signs of dehydration develop.
    - No medications (antidiarrheals or antibiotics) were started during this consult.
- Issue 2: Asthma history (uncertain current status; patient reports using an inhaler described as “Lexapro”)
  - Assessment:
    - Asthma history reported but current control/status and inhaler details unclear/conflict noted.
  - Plan:
    - No specific asthma treatment changes or plans documented in this consult.
- Issue 3: Preventive / follow-up
  - Assessment:
    - Risk stratification provided verbally (indications for stool testing, dehydration/hospitalization).
  - Plan:
    - Patient advised to contact service or seek care if worsening per return precautions; information recorded in app for patient review.

General Plan items:
- Documented advice and education provided in-app for patient to review.
- No prescriptions, laboratory tests, or imaging ordered during this consult.
